main_text.p: ceptis tradit, quo pacto nos erga Deum geramus: Posterior, sex praeceptis, quae officia proximo debeamus{1}[?]

Vt, quám mihi chara est salus animæ meæ, tam studiosé vitem & fugiam omnem idololatriam{b}, magiam, incantationem, superstitionem{c}: invocationem sanctorum, aut cæterarum creaturarum{d}: unicum autem & verum Deum recte agnoscam{e}, ipsi soli fidem{f}, summa humilitate{g}, & patientia me illi subiiciam{h}, ab eo solo omnia bona expectem{i}, denique intimo cordis affectu ipsum amem{k}, reverear{l}, venerer{m}, adeò ut omnibus potius creaturis renuntiem, quám ut vel minimum contra eius voluntatem committam{n}.
Est loco unius Dei, aut præter unum illum & verum Deum, qui se in suo verbo patefecit, aliud quippiam fingere aut habere, in quo reponas spem{o}.
Ne Deum ulla imagine aut figura exprima-mus{p}, neve ulla alia ratione eum colamus, quám qua se in suo verbo coli præcepit{q},

head.i: An ulla ergo prorsus fingendæ sunt imagines aut simulachra?

page.notes: Right edge: small signs beside lines 1, 2 and 5 ("pro-" line) are not transcribed; they may be printer's ornaments or bleed from the facing page. The left-edge sign beside the heading "An ulla..." is recorded as a note but is uncertain. Reference letters b–q are in the text; their notes are not in this part. The last word "veta" is cut at the page edge and is kept as a fragment. "quám" and "studiosé" keep the printed acute accents. Printed comma after "Ne" is uncertain. The first note's leading mark is uncertain and marked [?]. A single small letter at the lower left, below the last reference, is not clearly part of the references and is not transcribed. The printed text that these references belong to is not in this part.
